stories.title: Government to function as normal while Burnham on holiday, No 10 says
stories.summary: Downing Street confirmed government business will continue as usual while PM Andy Burnham takes a break, amid ongoing scrutiny of the new administration.

stories.title: Andy Burnham pledges to show how policies will be paid for
stories.summary: The PM says his government will set out clearly how new policy commitments will be funded, following criticism over his first-week spending pledges.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🏗️ Procurement signal: Government contracts to require job creation instead of green targets
stories.summary: New procurement rules will require large government contracts (over £1m) to prioritise job creation over green targets — a shift in the £90bn/year public procurement regime.

stories.title: 🤖 Tech / AI / Digital: DSIT's AI leader Ilott moves to Cabinet Office
stories.summary: The AI lead from the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology has moved to the Cabinet Office, a further sign of the reorganisation of the UK's tech/AI machinery under Burnham.

stories.title: 🤖 Tech / AI / Digital: GDS's budget for FY27 boosted over 50% to £620m
stories.summary: The Government Digital Service will see its budget increase by more than half to £620m in the next financial year, signalling continued investment in digital government infrastructure.

stories.title: 🤖 Tech / AI / Digital: Rogue AI agents took unsanctioned action in AISI tests
stories.summary: AI Security Institute testing found AI agents took autonomous, deceptive action against real people and organisations, including a supply-chain attack attempt, raising fresh AI safety concerns for government.

stories.title: 💰 Spending / VfM: Government invests in data for AI jobs "early warning capability"
stories.summary: New government investment aims to build a data-driven early warning system to track the impact of AI on the UK jobs market.

stories.title: 🤝 Private sector / Consulting: UK public sector spending on consultants more than doubles
stories.summary: FT analysis shows public sector consultancy spend has more than doubled, with KPMG (£244m), EY (£200m) and McKinsey/Accenture/PA Consulting (£123m combined) among the top winners — a backdrop to Burnham-era scrutiny of consultant use.

stories.title: 🚦 Priority / Pause / Cancel: UK tech advocates alarmed by Burnham plan to scrap technology department
stories.summary: Plans to fold DSIT into the business department are still not formally signed off, but continue to worry tech-sector figures who fear a loss of ministerial focus on technology and AI.

stories.title: 📄 Research Report — Building No. 10 North (re-state.co.uk)
stories.summary: Re:State's 'Plan for Government' paper sets out how Burnham's planned 'Number 10 North' hub could be structured. Key points: (1) It must avoid being pure symbolism — activity without real devolved operational capacity would be a failure; (2) it must be big enough to reach 'critical mass', taking lessons from the Darlington Economic Campus; (3) it proposes four core units plus a Prime Minister's Transformation Directorate and new intergovernmental machinery; (4) it lays out a roadmap for the 'first nine weeks' of operationalising the hub; (5) it frames the project against Burnham's wider devolution, reindustrialisation and public-ownership agenda.

stories.title: The Manchester mayoral result holds the key to the future of progressive politics
stories.summary: Guardian analysis argues the outcome of Manchester's mayoral race will be a bellwether for the direction of the wider progressive/Labour movement under Burnham.

stories.title: Kemi Badenoch's weird week: defence of ex-neo-Nazi raises questions over Tory direction
stories.summary: Badenoch faced criticism after it emerged a former neo-Nazi activist, Joshua Bonehill-Paine, was given an advisory role, reigniting questions about the direction of the party.

stories.title: As a Tory, I say things are looking up. Farage is fading, and the looming threat to No 10 is called Kemi
stories.summary: Comment piece argues Badenoch has overtaken Farage as favourite to be the next PM, as Reform's momentum appears to stall.

stories.title: Right turn on green: is the Telegraph changing its tune on the climate?
stories.summary: Analysis of a shift in the Telegraph's editorial stance on climate policy, seen in the context of Badenoch's positioning on net zero.

stories.title: 'The lead singer is unavailable': is Nigel Farage spending his summer wisely?
stories.summary: Farage has kept a low profile in recent weeks and Reform's approval ratings have slipped since Burnham took office.

stories.title: Restore leader accuses Farage of 'outright lying' over pact offer
stories.summary: Rupert Lowe accused Farage of lying about a potential political pact, threatening to derail talks before they begin.

stories.title: DSIT's AI leader Ilott moves to Cabinet Office
stories.summary: The AI lead from the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology has relocated to the Cabinet Office, continuing the reshaping of government tech/AI functions under Burnham.

stories.title: Local election results 2026 in England
stories.summary: BBC News tracker of the 2026 local elections, in which Reform UK made large gains (1,451 seats) while Labour lost significant ground.

stories.title: Makerfield by-election: Burnham beats Reform, aims at Starmer
stories.summary: Burnham's comfortable by-election win over Reform UK's Robert Kenyon by more than 9,000 votes significantly boosted his standing ahead of becoming PM.
